questions: What product feedback and customer themes exist for Connect right now?
What has changed in the personal-CRM / relationship-management market recently?
Who are the live competitors and how do they differentiate?
What does new user behavior in this space suggest about unmet needs?
What opportunities, if any, are worth flagging to Head of Product?

findings.finding: Connect has no first-party customer feedback or usage data to review. Phase 1 leaves apps/connect/ deliberately empty — the app scaffold itself is Phase 2 work — so there are zero live users and zero product surface to have generated feedback.

The only live internal signal this cycle is engineering/process friction, not customer signal: GitHub issue #34 documents that the Deploy charter describes a QA-verdict gate at deploy time that tools/deploy-verify cannot enforce. It is real and open, but it is a Security/Release/QA concern, not a product-opportunity finding, so it is noted here and not adopted as a Research recommendation.
sources: https://github.com (repo) issue #34: "Deploy charter specifies behaviour tools/deploy-verify cannot perform; QA-verdict gate is dead at deploy time"

findings.finding: The personal-CRM category is mature and crowded, with 60+ tracked entrants as of 2026. The visible leaders differentiate on distinct axes: Dex on LinkedIn-native enrichment and job-change alerts; Clay/Mesh on contact enrichment for high-value professional networks; Monica on open-source, self-hosted data ownership; Folk on team/shared-network collaboration; Covve on mobile-first phone-contact enrichment.

Category-wide, 2026 CRM trends are agentic AI moving from pilot to rollout, mobile access reaching ~58.7% of usage, rising voice-AI adoption, and a shift from flat subscriptions to hybrid free-plus-premium-AI-tier pricing. Professionals/consultants/sales roles remain the dominant end-user segment (~49.3%).

Almost every mainstream personal-CRM competitor is built around professional networking or sales use cases. A separate, smaller cluster of apps (amiqo, Fabriq, Bubblic, Waffle, Intriq) targets non-professional relationship maintenance (friends, family), but coverage is fragmented across communication apps, journal apps, and light CRM-style nudging tools — none unify both halves of the problem. One source frames it directly: friendship maintenance has two separate problems, remembering to reach out and remembering what to say, and most tools only address the first, and address it badly.

This market has a specific failure pattern worth treating as a warning, not just a trend: attempts at a general-purpose "CRM for your life" have been made for over 15 years and most no longer exist. Named churn drivers for CRM-style apps generally are crashes/bugs (cited by 50.3% of users as a deal-breaker), manual data-entry burden, and unclear value versus price — all of which point at effort-to-maintain, not feature count, as the likely failure mode for this category.

optionsConsidered.option: Position Connect to compete directly in professional-networking personal-CRM (Dex/Clay/Folk territory).
optionsConsidered.assessment: Crowded and infrastructure-heavy (LinkedIn integration, contact enrichment pipelines) for a pre-launch entrant with no build yet; weak differentiation against incumbents with multi-year data moats.

optionsConsidered.option: Narrow toward non-professional relationship maintenance (friends, family, mentors) — closing the "remembering what to say" half that the current fragmented field leaves unsolved.
optionsConsidered.assessment: Smaller, less-crowded field and matches the charter already on record for Connect (docs/roles/research.md: "how people actually maintain the relationships Connect is for"). The 15-year graveyard of general life-CRM attempts is a real risk signal: the finding above suggests manual upkeep effort, not missing features, is what has killed prior entrants, so this option is only sound if paired with near-zero manual data entry.

optionsConsidered.option: Take no product-direction action this cycle; wait for Phase 2 to ship before gathering any feedback.
optionsConsidered.assessment: Defensible given there is genuinely no live product to survey yet, but it wastes the nightly cadence's only lever — flagging pre-build risk before Product commits a spec — when a specific, sourced risk (manual-entry churn) is already visible and cheap to record now.

recommendation: No build action this cycle — evidence is thin because Connect has no live users, and this scan is not the mechanism that commissions builds. The one actionable item is a proposal for Head of Product to weigh when Connect's spec is written: if Connect's future scope leans toward personal (non-sales) relationship maintenance, the sourced risk above is manual data-entry burden, historically the primary reason general 'life CRM' products have failed over 15+ years, so any spec in that direction should treat near-zero manual upkeep as a hard constraint rather than a nice-to-have, and should not compete on the same axis as Dex/Clay/Folk. This is flagged to Head of Product as input, not adopted as a decision.
